start.speaker: Aide
start.text: Welcome to the Office of Municipal Reclamation. You're dripping on the marble. How may I direct your... concern?

n1.speaker: Aide
n1.text: Please keep it brief. The Office values everyone's time equally, which is to say, not at all.

choices.text: I want to see the Reclamation Board.
People are dying in the harbor districts.

board.speaker: Aide
board.text: The Board doesn't take appointments, detective. The Board doesn't take anything — it reviews, it allocates, it reclaims. There's no man behind the curtain. There's a committee, and committees don't have faces to punch. Would you like a pamphlet?

discover.title: There Is No Man
discover.desc: The aide explains, pleasantly, that the Reclamation Board is a committee — no chair you can name, no face you can hold accountable. Decisions arrive from it the way weather does. You came looking for a villain and found a procedure.

dying.speaker: Aide
dying.text: Yes. That's logged. 'Sub-standard water outcomes, harbor sector.' It's a Tier-Three municipal concern — there's a form, 27-B, if you'd like to add a statement. Current response time is... indefinite. His smile doesn't move when he says it. Is there anything else?

r9.speaker: Aide
r9.text: Order R-9 is a routine sanitation allocation. Sealed, per policy. I can't tell you who signed it. And honestly, aide to aide? Neither could the person who signed it — it came up through channels, initialled at each desk, no single hand responsible at any point. That's not a cover-up, detective. That's just how the building breathes.

bye.speaker: Aide
bye.text: Mind the steps on your way out. They're original marble. We do so hate to see them stained.
